thread:
marta: FYI i prototyped an "ownership-fallback + shadow-cache" flow to harden demote/evict decisions during rapid handoffs. idea: if ownership metadata might be stale, we avoid immediate demote and instead move prefixes into a node-local shadow (read-only) for a short TTL while we confirm ownership. results from a short replay below.

kevin: sounds neat. how is shadow different from the rehydrate LRU we've used?

marta: shadow-cache stores a compact serialized slab of the model KV for the prefix (not full memory copy) and is intended to serve reads for very short windows (rehydrate_ttl_shallow=5-20s). key differences:
- it's written atomically at demote time (so no race where demote removes live cache before snapshot)
- includes an ownership_proof token (seq + sig) to correlate with ownership service state
- serves only GETs and marks reads as "served_from_shadow" in telemetry

yusuf: how do we get the ownership_proof? doesn't that add RPCs to hot path?

marta: ownership service emits signed short-lived proofs via the existing gossip stream. runtime caches them; on demote path we attach the proof to the shadow snapshot. the proof is used later if another node tries to claim the prefix quickly; it's authoritative for a small window and avoids hitting origin while ownership settles. no extra RPCs on hot path, just cached proofs. pseudocode: 

marta: ```
# demote handler (hot path)
if !ownership_cache.is_stable(prefix):
  # instead of immediate demote->evict, take shadow snapshot
  snap = take_compact_snapshot(prefix)
  snap.attach(ownership_cache.get_proof(prefix))
  shadow_cache.put(prefix, snap, ttl=shadow_ttl)
  mark_shadowed(prefix)
else:
  evict(prefix)
```

tara: interesting. correctness: can shadow serve stale reads after a write races in? what if a write happens right after we snapshot?

marta: invariant: we only serve shadow reads if shadow.snapshot_proof.seq == ownership_service.current_seq(prefix) OR if a fast revalidation to ownership service confirms the proof. We also keep a write_pin on any recent writes and block snapshot creation if last_write_age < write_pin_ttl. snapshots are intentionally conservative: they include a watermark last_write_ts and we reject serving if a read's trace indicates it may be a write.

kevin: logs / example?

marta: sanitized run:
```
[2026-08-01T12:00:01Z] demote_eval: prefix=cfg-xyz tenant=team-neo reason=probabilistic ownership_cached=false -> shadow_snapshot created ttl=15s proof_seq=992
[2026-08-01T12:00:02Z] shadow_hit: prefix=cfg-xyz tenant=team-neo served_from=shadow latency=6ms
[2026-08-01T12:00:03Z] ownership_update: prefix=cfg-xyz new_seq=993 -> proof mismatch, runtime fetched new_proof and promoted to local cache
[2026-08-01T12:00:04Z] shadow_expire: prefix=cfg-xyz ttl=15s -> removed
```

yusuf: what about the cost impact (extra snapshotting CPU / storage)?

marta: snapshots are compact by design (delta-encoded or compressed) and we only snapshot for prefixes with eviction probability > threshold and where ownership_cache.is_unknown. on our 4-host canary (6h) CPU increased ~1.6% and disk ops negligible; token egress down 9.5%. most snapshots were small (64-512B) since prefix values are small config blobs.

tara: ops telemetry and alerts?

marta: added: shadow_snapshot_created, shadow_hit, shadow_serve_latency, shadow_promote_on_proof, shadow_reject_on_write_pin. alerts: if shadow_to_origin_miss_rate > 2% for 10m, pause shadowing; if shadow_cpu_overhead > 5% for 5m, rollback.

kevin: tests?

marta: test plan:
- unit: proof attach/verify + snapshot atomicity
- property: interleave write/handoff/demote with deterministic RNG and assert no read-observed stale-writes
- integration: canary 1% multi-tenant hosts with shadow_ttl sweep 5/15/30s, measure demote_to_origin_count and read-after-write regressions

deploy-bot: canary plan -> group=shadow-evict-canary hosts=shadow-1..shadow-3 start=2026-08-02T01:00:00Z

yusuf: one more edge: what if many nodes create shadows for same prefix and they proliferate slightly increasing memory use?

marta: shadow_cache is bounded per-node (max_shadows=1024) and we fold duplicates: snapshots include prefix fingerprint; when a node receives a snapshot with same fingerprint it dedups and extends TTL only if new_proof.seq > existing.seq. also prefer in-memory dedupe to avoid duplicates.

tara: recommended invariants to document?

marta: yes: "Shadow snapshot may be created iff ownership_cache.unknown AND last_write_age > write_pin_ttl AND snapshot_quota_available" and "Shadow may serve reads only if proof_seq == current_seq OR revalidated by ownership service; shadow serves reads only for GETs, not writes." i'll add these to the runtime README and tie unit tests to them. opening PR with flags: enable_shadow, shadow_ttl, max_shadows, snapshot_threshold. comments welcome.
